content:
Rumors suggest Apple's fall iPhone lineup this year will revolve around two models: the iPhone 18 Pro and the iPhone Ultra. Below are the three most important feature differences—setting aside price—that could influence your decision on whether to upgrade.

Design: Traditional vs. Foldable

This difference is the most obvious, but worth mentioning because it is also the most significant distinction.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will retain the basic design that iPhones have used for years. Reportedly, the screen size and overall appearance will be identical to the previous generation. If you want the feel of a traditional iPhone, the iPhone 18 Pro will be your top choice.

As for the iPhone Ultra, it will be Apple's first foldable phone. Its body design is entirely different—the outer screen is shorter and wider than a traditional iPhone, while the inner screen resembles an iPad mini.

Cameras: Pro Models Still Reign Supreme

Apple has always poured its most cutting-edge and innovative camera technology into the Pro models. This year will continue that tradition.

The iPhone Ultra is expected to feature roughly the same camera capabilities as the iPhone 18 Pro, with one major exception: it will not have a telephoto lens.

There are rumors that the iPhone Ultra will still carry the same main lens, ultra-wide lens, and front-facing camera as the Pro series. However, the telephoto lens will remain exclusive to the Pro models, and is expected to be even better this year.

Performance: Both Feature the A20 Pro Chip, but Materials Affect Performance

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra are both expected to use the A20 Pro chip as their core. However, due to differences in design and materials, performance levels may vary.

The iPhone 18 Pro will continue the unibody aluminum design introduced on the iPhone 17 Pro, also equipped with a vapor chamber for cooling. These two changes made the iPhone 17 Pro's overall performance better than its predecessor, as the phone can stay cooler under heavy workloads.

The iPhone Ultra will adopt a slim titanium design similar to the iPhone Air. It may also feature a vapor chamber, though currently only one leaker has made this claim. However, due to the different materials used, even though the iPhone Ultra and iPhone 18 Pro share the same chip, performance may be slightly inferior under direct sunlight or during intensive operations.
